rationale: The workflow already implements the high-impact optimizations supported by the evidence: concurrency with cancel-in-progress (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE, 1.9-4.1% VM reduction), explicit job timeouts on all jobs (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT, 12.9/8.1% VM reduction), and likely dependency caching via the custom setup-pnpm action (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE, 6/3.4% VM reduction). The experiment evidence (batch-interactive-three) demonstrates adding a timeout where none existed, but this workflow already has timeouts (5-20 min) on every job. Remaining patterns show minimal aggregate impact (<0.1% for path filtering, workflow skipping) or require CI-service changes not expressible in workflow YAML (P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST, P-LIT-BUILD-PRIORITY). Without per-job historical duration data, reducing existing timeouts risks false failures and lacks direct evidence support. The current configuration preserves all build/test coverage and follows evidenced best practices.
